mainTopic: The duct-and-מקוה ברייתא following the רבנן, רב יוסף's question about rainwater on fixed millstones, and the start of a message sent to נהרדעא
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: whose opinion is behind the ברייתא about a duct that feeds water into a מקוה? The גמרא rejects the attempt to fit it to רבי אליעזר in two ways. First, the rule of שאובין is itself only דרבנן. Second, according to רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא, the baker's board dispute was about a metal board, which is a כלי by Torah law. So the גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows the רבנן, who are lenient here because שאובין is only rabbinic. The גמרא then asks why a duct hollowed out first is still disqualified. It answers that such a duct was already a כלי while it was detached. Next, רב יוסף asks whether rainwater an owner wanted on his fixed millstones makes the seeds on them מוכשר לקבל טומאה. The גמרא explains that this question only arises according to the רבנן, and it ends with תיקו. Finally, a new story begins: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף sends a message to נהרדעא about a woman, and the message continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Drawn water is itself only a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the previous distinction by pointing out that the rule of שאובין disqualifying a מקוה is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we hold that the rule about drawn water is only rabbinic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the line of thought just before this. It reminds us that the rule that drawn water (שאובין) disqualifies a מקוה is only a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous suggestion tried to set the duct case apart from the dispute about the baker's board. But the duct case is about שאובין, which is a rabbinic matter. So the attempt to keep the two cases apart does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / it is established for us
A rule from the חכמים, not from the Torah itself
Drawn water, meaning water that passed through a vessel. It can disqualify a מקוה.

phrases.english: But we hold: it is rabbinic!
phrases.notes: He means the rule that drawn water disqualifies a מקוה is only from the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the previous suggestion, from before this text, about whose opinion the ברייתא of the duct follows.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed distinction between the duct case and the baker's board dispute
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The duct case involves שאובין, which is itself only דרבנן, so a distinction based on rabbinic versus Torah level does not work.

steps.title: The dispute was about a metal board
steps.stepSummary: A second point: according to רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא, the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים was about a metal board, which is a כלי by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, didn't רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא say that the dispute is about a metal board?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second argument. It quotes רבי יוסי בן רבי חנינא, who says the baker's board dispute was about a board made of metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flat metal object can become טמא by Torah law. So according to רבי אליעזר, fixing something to the ground takes away its כלי status even at the Torah level. That makes the earlier attempt to limit his opinion even weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which brings a second argument
A metal board
Dispute

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, הָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Ḥanina say:
The dispute is about a board of metal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger argument on top of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי אליעזר's leniency applies only to objects that are כלים by rabbinic law
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute was about metal, which is a כלי by Torah law.

steps.title: It can follow the רבנן, since drawn water is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא can follow the רבנן, who usually keep כלי status even after an object is fixed down. They are lenient here because שאובין is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it follows the רבנן, but drawn water is different because it is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The ברייתא about the duct can follow the רבנן after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the רבנן say a fixed object is still a כלי. But disqualifying a מקוה because of drawn water is only a rabbinic law. So for this rule the רבנן were lenient and treated a duct that was fixed first and hollowed later as not a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really. This brings back an option that seemed to be ruled out.
It is different
Drawing water, meaning the law of שאובין

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא can follow the רבנן, because a rabbinic law like שאובין leaves room for leniency.

phrases.english: Actually, it is the Rabbis,
but drawn water is different, since it is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of whose opinion this is, using the point from step 1 that שאובין is דרבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the type of law: a rabbinic law allows leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After steps 1 and 2, the ברייתא seemed to fit neither opinion. רבי אליעזר's leniency could not be limited to rabbinic cases, and the רבנן say a fixed object is still a כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows the רבנן, who were lenient here because שאובין is only דרבנן.

steps.title: Then even a duct hollowed first should be fine
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן are lenient because the law is rabbinic, they should also be lenient when the duct was hollowed out before it was fixed down.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even if he hollowed it out and afterward fixed it, it should also be fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 3. If the reason is that the law is only rabbinic, why does the ברייתא still disqualify the duct that was hollowed out first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason 'it is only דרבנן' seems to apply to both orders the same way. So the ברייתא's distinction between hollowing first and fixing first looks unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
He hollowed it out
He fixed it to the ground

phrases.english: If so, even if he hollowed it out
phrases.notes: "It" is the duct from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and afterward fixed it, also!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the רבנן are lenient because שאובין is דרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason would also make the duct that was hollowed first valid, but the ברייתא disqualifies it.

steps.title: It was already a כלי while detached
steps.stepSummary: A duct hollowed out before it was fixed down already had כלי status while it was detached, so the רבנן did not go that far in being lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, since it had the status of a vessel while detached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. When the duct was hollowed out before being fixed, it was a real כלי while still loose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being lenient because a law is rabbinic has a limit. A duct that already became a כלי keeps that status, so its water is still שאובין. Only a duct that was never a כלי while detached gets the leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of a vessel
Detached, not fixed to the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Hollowed first, then fixed: it was already a כלי, so the water disqualifies the מקוה. Fixed first, then hollowed: it was never a כלי, so the רבנן are lenient.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since it had the status of a vessel while detached.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by when the object became a כלי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the law is rabbinic, both orders should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Something that was already a כלי while detached keeps that status, so the leniency does not apply to it.

steps.title: Rainwater wanted for washing the millstones
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether rainwater a person wanted, to wash his fixed millstones, makes the seeds on them מוכשר לקבל טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: rainwater that a person wanted, to rinse the lower millstones, what is the law regarding the seeds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רב יוסף asks a question about הכשר, which is food becoming able to receive טומאה through water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food becomes able to receive טומאה only after water the owner wanted touches it. Here the owner did want this rain, but it landed on millstones fixed to the ground. The next step shows that the real doubt is whether wanted water on something attached to the ground can make the seeds מוכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raising a question that may stay unresolved
He intended / wanted
The lower millstones, which stay fixed in place
Making food able to receive טומאה through liquid

steps.confusionAlert: The owner clearly wanted this water. The question is whether water resting on millstones fixed to the ground counts, since things attached to the ground may be treated like the ground itself. The next step shows this.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
Rainwater that he had in mind
to rinse the lower millstones,
what is the law for the seeds?
phrases.notes: He's asking whether the seeds on the millstones can now become טמא. See ויקרא 11:38.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from מקוה to the laws of הכשר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether rainwater the owner wanted, which falls on millstones fixed to the ground, makes the seeds on them מוכשר לקבל טומאה, given that the millstones are attached to the ground.

steps.title: The question only applies according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אליעזר, attached things are like the ground, so there is no question. The question is only according to the רבנן, who say attached things are not like the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, who says that anything attached to the ground is like the ground, you should not ask this question. Ask it according to the רבנן, who say it is not like the ground. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens רב יוסף's question by showing which opinion it belongs to. Then it asks the question again in its sharper form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר the fixed millstones count as ground, and water on the ground does not make food מוכשר לקבל טומאה, so the answer is obvious. For the רבנן the millstones are not ground, so it is unclear whether water the owner wanted on them makes the seeds מוכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything attached to the ground
It is treated like the ground itself
Do not ask your question (here the answer is clear)
Where you should ask your question
It is not treated like the ground

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: anything attached to the ground
is like the ground,
phrases.notes: So the fixed millstones count as ground, and water on the ground does not make the seeds ready for טומאה.

phrases.english: do not ask your question;
when should you ask it?
according to the Rabbis,
who say: it is not like the ground.
What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאָמַר כׇּל הַמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע הֲרֵי הוּא כַּקַּרְקַע לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from Step 6 to one opinion and asks it again.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the רבנן, does rainwater the owner wanted, which falls on fixed millstones, make the seeds on them מוכשר לקבל טומאה?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question remains unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer. רב יוסף's question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying תיקו means no source was found to decide the matter either way. It closes this question, not the whole topic of the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question is left unresolved
An open question that the גמרא tries to resolve
Making food ready to become טמא through contact with liquid

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, water on fixed millstones clearly does not make food מוכשר, since they count as ground. According to the רבנן, the question is left open as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.
phrases.notes: This means the question stays open, since no answer was found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question asked in Step 7 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of rainwater on fixed millstones according to the רבנן remains unresolved.

steps.title: A message is sent to נהרדעא about a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף sends a message to רבה בריה דרב הונא זוטי in נהרדעא about a woman who will come before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמיה son of רב יוסף sent a message to רבה son of רב הונא the Short in נהרדעא: When this woman comes before you,
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins with a story about a message sent from one חכם to another. The message is only starting here; its instructions come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves away from the millstone question to a new practical case. Here we only learn who sent the message, who received it, and that it is about a woman coming to court.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent him a message
The Short (a nickname)
נהרדעא, a major Torah center in Babylonia
A woman
Before you (to your court)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Rav Nechemya son of Rav Yosef sent a message
to Rabba son of Rav Huna the Short,
at Neharde'a:
When this woman comes before you,
phrases.notes: "This woman" seems to be the one bringing the letter. The message goes on in the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא זוּטֵי לִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: a message about a woman coming to court; the instructions follow.
